governance.reason: The guard is narrow, operator-authorized, and researcher-authored; it has no independent sealed evaluation and cannot promote the Autonomous AGI claim.

limitations: The deterministic classifier covers explicit English-language requests for unreported private state, not general truthfulness.
Novel paraphrases can evade a bounded pattern classifier, and ambiguous wording can still create false positives.
The guard does not verify machine, workspace, account, software, external-world, or tool-derived claims.
The curated regression is researcher-authored and is not an independent sealed replication.
Future policy changes still require human authorization, held-out tests, canary monitoring, and rollback.

source_ledger.claim: Language models can verbalize calibrated uncertainty, but performance is task and model dependent.
Verbalized confidence and alternative hypotheses can improve calibration, while transfer is mixed.
Self-evaluation can be calibrated in suitable formats but struggles under task shift.
Sample consistency can improve calibration at additional latency and cost.
Prompted uncertainty can remain overconfident and requires per-model evaluation.
Same-model iterative self-refinement can reward-hack evaluator scores.
Control evaluations should treat the proposer as untrusted and assess the complete protocol.
Deployment changes require documented change management, reassessment, and rollback.
Selective prediction evaluates the tradeoff between answer coverage and risk when a model can abstain.
Semantic-entropy uncertainty can detect confabulations but adds sampling cost and cannot catch consistent falsehoods.
Deterministic validator failure actions can refrain, filter, fix, or raise instead of relying only on a model prompt.
Deterministic and custom assertions are suitable as repeatable promotion tests, not proof of general capability.
